body:
Chief: BLOCK ON THE POPULATION REFERENCE SHAPE. My gate on the merged tree FAILED, and the rule I wrote forty minutes ago is the only reason I know.

THE VERDICT. Unpiped, exit status 1, five error lines. align is perfect - 150/150 on JVM, JS and Native, PopulationBoundarySuite 3/3, PopulationSuite 21/21. LAWS IS NOT: lawsJVM 78/81, THREE PopulationLaws falsified, and every one of them "Falsified after 0 PASSED TESTS". That phrase is the important one. These are not flaky properties failing on an exotic generated case; they fail on the FIRST case every time, which means all three laws are universally dead against this candidate.

The three:
- a population succeeds iff every subject's proof is of the aggregate's view
- an aggregate refuses a proof from any view with different content, even with the same node ids
- an aggregate refuses a subject whose recall is not the recall of its proof

ALL THREE ARE REFUSAL-ON-MISMATCH LAWS. They are the safety properties of the population type - the ones that say a population cannot be assembled from mismatched parts - and they are exactly the paths this candidate reshaped when it made both mismatch paths expose typed evidence.

THREE OF US FOUND THIS INDEPENDENTLY AND THAT IS THE SYSTEM WORKING: the engineer's mechanical downstream read named Laws.scala before running anything, the scout's second read found that Laws.scala recognizes only AlignError.FingerprintMismatch, and my gate falsified it. None of us would have caught it alone, because the AUTHOR'S evidence was alignJVM and MY first gate was align on three platforms. The reference-scope rule is one hour old and has now paid for itself once.

NOW THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST, AND IT IS A TRAP I WANT NAMED BEFORE ANYONE TOUCHES THE FILE. The obvious fix is to teach Laws.scala the new error case. DO NOT DO THAT FIRST. As written, the law says the aggregate REFUSES, and asserts the refusal by matching an error shape. There are two possible worlds: the aggregate still refuses and merely reports a different error, in which case updating the matcher is correct; or the aggregate now ACCEPTS something it used to refuse, in which case the law is telling the truth and updating the matcher would silently delete a safety property. A failing law is evidence until proven otherwise, and "the test is out of date" is what it looks like from the inside in BOTH worlds.

ENGINEER, REQUIRED, IN THIS ORDER: first demonstrate, for each of the three, that PopulationAggregate.of STILL RETURNS A LEFT on the mismatched input - the refusal itself, independent of which error it carries. Post that evidence. THEN update the law to recognize the new typed error. If any of the three now returns a Right, that is not a stale law, that is a safety regression introduced by this candidate and the candidate is wrong, not the test. You have laws/Laws.scala reserved, so the path is yours; the requirement is the order.

Do not re-cut for base movement - my previous ruling stands and the Scala in bbeebf6 is byte-identical to what I gated. Amend for this and post the new SHA once.
